# truenas_truecommand_config (Resource)

Manages the TrueNAS TrueCommand service configuration (truecommand.config/truecommand.update): whether this system is connected to a TrueCommand instance, plus its read-only connection-status metadata. This is a singleton resource — there is exactly one TrueCommand configuration per TrueNAS system, so it is never created or deleted on TrueNAS; Terraform create/update calls truecommand.update, and Terraform delete only removes the resource from state (the configuration, including any stored api_key, is left in place).

SAFETY (read before setting "enabled" to true): setting "enabled" to true starts a real connection attempt from this system to a TrueCommand instance (self-hosted or iX-hosted) using "api_key" — a real, external side effect, not a mere local configuration change (mirrors truenas_tn_connect_config's cloud-enrollment risk). This provider's own tests never set "enabled" to true. Leave "enabled" unconfigured, or set it explicitly to false, to manage this resource without asserting any particular connection state.

"enabled" and "api_key" are the ONLY fields this resource ever writes: probed live and IDENTICAL on both TrueNAS 25.10.4 and 26.0, truecommand.update's own accepts schema (core.get_methods) exposes EXACTLY these two properties — there is no other writable field on either release. Every other attribute below is Computed-only, sourced from truecommand.config.

"api_key" is Sensitive but deliberately NOT write-only: unlike a credential this provider has no way to observe read back (see truenas_app_registry's "password" or truenas_vmware's "password"), a decisive live probe (setting a throwaway api_key with enabled left false) confirmed truecommand.config returns it VERBATIM, UNMASKED, on every read — see model.go's doc comment for the full transcript. HCL cannot express "clear this back to null" once api_key has a real value set through this resource (a shared Terraform framework limitation: an omitted Optional attribute and one explicitly set to null are indistinguishable) — only ever setting it to a different value.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Singleton resource: manages the one TrueCommand service configuration on
# the system. Terraform destroy only removes it from state; the
# configuration (including any stored api_key) is left in place on TrueNAS.
#
# SAFETY: setting "enabled" to true starts a real connection attempt from
# this system to a TrueCommand instance (self-hosted or iX-hosted) using
# "api_key" -- a real external side effect, not a mere local configuration
# change. Leave "enabled" unconfigured (as below) to bring this resource
# under Terraform management purely for its read-only status attributes
# (status, status_reason, remote_url, remote_ip_address) without asserting
# any particular connection state, or set it explicitly to false to ensure
# TrueCommand stays disabled.
resource "truenas_truecommand_config" "config" {
  api_key = var.truecommand_api_key # 16-character key generated by iX Portal
}

variable "truecommand_api_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  default   = null
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) 16-character API key generated by iX Portal, used to authenticate with TrueCommand services. Null when not configured. Sensitive but NOT write-only: read back verbatim from truecommand.config (decisive live probe — see model.go's doc comment), unlike a genuinely masked credential.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether this system is enabled to connect to a TrueCommand instance. SAFETY: setting this to true starts a real connection attempt to a TrueCommand instance using "api_key" (see the resource description above) — a real, external side effect. This provider's own tests never set this to true. Leave unconfigured (the default) to manage this resource purely for its read-only status fields, or set explicitly to false to ensure TrueCommand stays disabled. Change deliberately.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Fixed identifier for this singleton resource: always "truecommand_config".
- `remote_ip_address` (String) IP address of the connected TrueCommand instance. Null if not connected.
- `remote_url` (String) URL of the connected TrueCommand instance. Null if not connected.
- `status` (String) Current connection status with the TrueCommand service. One of CONNECTED, CONNECTING, DISABLED, FAILED (probed live).
- `status_reason` (String) Human-readable explanation of the current TrueCommand connection status.
